mailypoppins

Write your mail in Vim and let your AI agent draft and proofread it.

mailypoppins is a keyboard-first mail client for macOS and Linux. It comes as a terminal app, a command-line tool and a Mac app.

Show a client
Terminal app
$ mp search --local 'from:ada invoice'
"from:ada invoice" in work (1 hit):
────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
[unread] mp://work/inbox/8c41f0e2@example.com → you@example.com
      Tue, 13 Oct 2026 09:12  Invoice 2026-114, site survey

$ mp reply mp://work/inbox/8c41f0e2@example.com
mp://work/drafts/3f9c27a1d4e8b605

$ mp edit mp://work/drafts/3f9c27a1d4e8b605  # opens in Neovim
$ mp list
Drafts:
────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
[draft] mp://work/drafts/3f9c27a1d4e8b605 → ada@example.com
      Re: Invoice 2026-114, site survey

$ mp mark-approved mp://work/drafts/3f9c27a1d4e8b605
$ mp send mp://work/drafts/3f9c27a1d4e8b605

Mailboxes, the message list and the reader sit side by side. The app also runs over SSH.

Keyboard-first email client

Read, triage and write without reaching for the mouse.

  • Write in your editor

    Every draft is a Markdown file that opens in your $EDITOR, Vim and Neovim included. The Mac app runs Neovim inside its window.

  • Vim keys throughout

    j and k, gg, / and a Space leader move you through mailboxes, threads and drafts.

  • All clients share one mailbox

    The terminal app, the command line and the Mac app work on the same mailbox. A change made in one appears in the others at once.

Built for efficient human-AI collaboration

Your agent works with the same commands and files you do, on your Mac or on a Linux server.

  • Context on demand

    Your agent searches your whole mail history for the information it needs to help you.

  • A co-author for your emails

    It proofreads and edits your drafts, or prepares replies for you to review. It edits the draft files themselves, without any copy and paste.

  • Stay updated

    Ask it which emails still wait for your answer.

mailypoppins sends a draft only after you mark it approved.

Technical details

Platforms
The Mac app runs on Apple silicon. The terminal app and the command line run on macOS and on Linux (x86_64).
Accounts
Any IMAP and SMTP provider works with a password, including Gmail, Proton Mail Bridge and on-premises Exchange. Microsoft 365 connects through the Graph API.
Calendar
mailypoppins sends meeting invitations and answers the ones you receive. Both use the standard iMIP format.
Storage
Drafts are Markdown files with YAML frontmatter. Received mail is stored in a local SQLite database with full-text search. You can read and search it offline.
Automation
mp list, mp search and mp show print JSON with --json. IMAP IDLE delivers new mail as it arrives. Hooks run your own command when a matching message comes in.
Stack
mailypoppins is written in Rust, with ratatui for the terminal app and Tauri for the Mac app. It is MIT licensed.

Get started

  1. 1

    Install

    The Mac app runs on Apple silicon, includes mp and updates itself.

    Download .dmg

    The app is not signed yet, so macOS asks you to allow it once in System Settings > Privacy & Security. The guide shows how.

    Homebrew installs the terminal app and the command line on macOS and Linux:

    bash 
    brew install sylvainHellin/mailypoppins/mailypoppins

    You can also download a binary for macOS arm64, Linux x86_64 or Linux x86_64 static.

  2. 2

    Add an account

    The Mac app asks for one on first launch. In a terminal, run mp config init. Any IMAP provider works, and so does Microsoft 365.

  3. 3

    Open your mail

    Open the Mac app, or run mp for the terminal app. The first sync starts on its own.
